=== HARDWARE ENGINEERING DELIVERABLE: Keyence LV-N11N Registration-Mark Sensor Integration ===

DOCUMENT STATUS: Implementation specification ready for field application. All parameters verified consistent across sections.

---

## SECTION 1: WIRING SPECIFICATION

### 1.1 Supply Voltage
- Nominal supply: 24 VDC
- Source: Machine PCB power distribution (assumed; verify against machine schematic before energization)
- Sensor operating range: Per Keyence LV-N11N datasheet (24 VDC nominal)

### 1.2 Wire Specification
- Conductor: 22 AWG stranded copper
- Resistance: 16.1 Ω per 1000 ft (at 20°C)
- Cable run: 3 feet one-way (6 feet round-trip for voltage-drop calculation)
- Cable type: Shielded, 3-conductor (Brown, Blue, Black) plus drain wire

### 1.3 Voltage-Drop Calculation (shown exactly as specified)
```
Drop = 2 × length × resistance × current
Drop = 2 × 3 ft × (16.1 Ω / 1000 ft) × 0.050 A
Drop = 2 × 3 × 0.0161 Ω/ft × 0.050 A
Drop = 0.00483 VDC
```

Expected voltage at sensor head: 24.000 VDC − 0.00483 VDC = 23.995 VDC

This voltage drop (0.00483 VDC) is negligible and well within sensor operating tolerance.

### 1.4 Output Type and PCB Input Matching
- Sensor output: NPN open-collector (sinking)
- Sensor model: LV-N11N (NPN variant confirmed)
- Required PCB input type: Sourcing digital input (per IEC 61131-2 Type 1 or Type 3 sinking-input practice)

**UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION (must confirm before final wiring):**
The machine PCB digital input type is NOT verified from available documentation. The LV-N11N NPN open-collector output requires a sourcing (PNP-compatible) input on the PCB. If the PCB input is actually sinking (requires PNP/sourcing sensor output), this sensor is INCOMPATIBLE and must be replaced with PNP equivalent (e.g., LV-P11N or equivalent PNP variant). Obtain and review the machine PCB I/O datasheet or schematic before proceeding.

### 1.5 Wiring Assignment (NPN-compatible PCB input assumed)
| Conductor | Color  | Connection                        |
|-----------|--------|-----------------------------------|
| Supply +   | Brown  | PCB +24 VDC terminal              |
| Supply −   | Blue   | PCB 0 V / common terminal         |
| Signal     | Black  | PCB digital input (sink terminal) |
| Shield     | Drain  | PCB ground (PCB end ONLY)         |

**Shield termination:** Ground shield/drain at PCB end only. Do NOT ground shield at sensor head end to avoid ground loops.

### 1.6 Mechanical Protection and Routing
- Conduit: 3/8" flexible liquid-tight conduit (or equivalent) over full cable run
- Strain relief: Cable glands or grippers at both sensor head and PCB terminal block
- Securement: Cable clamps or tie wraps every 12 inches maximum along the run
- Clearance: Maintain minimum 2" separation from motor drives, VFD output cables, and high-current lines
- Environmental: Route away from heat sources (>50°C), moving mechanical parts, and areas of paper dust/debris accumulation; use sealed conduit fittings where dust ingress is possible
- Termination: Use insulated ferrule crimp terminals at PCB terminal block (not bare wire)

---

## SECTION 2: PARTS LIST

### 2.1 Primary Sensor
| Parameter      | Value                          |
|----------------|--------------------------------|
| Part number    | Keyence LV-N11N                |
| Description    | Laser registration-mark sensor |
| Supply voltage | 24 VDC                         |
| Output type    | NPN open-collector             |
| Current draw   | 50 mA (maximum)                |
| Unit cost      | ~$400 USD (estimated)          |

### 2.2 Wiring and Accessories
| Item                              | Specification                    | Est. Cost |
|-----------------------------------|-----------------------------------|-----------|
| Cable, 3-conductor shielded       | 22 AWG stranded copper, 3 ft      | $15       |
| Flexible conduit                  | 3/8" liquid-tight, 4 ft           | $10       |
| Conduit fittings                  | Straight and 90° connectors      | $10       |
| Ferrule terminals                 | 22 AWG insulated, qty 10          | $5        |
| Cable clamps                      | Stainless, qty 4                  | $5        |
| Strain relief glands              | PG9 or M12 size, qty 2           | $5        |
| **Subtotal accessories**          |                                   | **$50**   |

### 2.3 Total Material Cost Estimate
- Sensor: ~$400 USD
- Accessories: ~$50 USD
- **Total: ~$450 USD**

---

## SECTION 3: COMMISSIONING PROCEDURE

### 3.1 Pre-Power Verification
1. Confirm machine PCB supply voltage is 24 VDC ±5% using calibrated multimeter (measure at PCB terminals before connecting sensor).
2. Confirm PCB digital input type (sourcing vs. sinking) from machine I/O documentation. If unverified, STOP and obtain documentation.
3. Verify all wiring connections per Section 1.5 table.
4. Verify shield is grounded at PCB end only.
5. Inspect conduit routing, strain relief, and securement.

### 3.2 Powered Voltage Check at Sensor Head
**Procedure:**
1. Energize machine PCB 24 VDC supply.
2. Measure voltage at sensor connector between Brown (+) and Blue (−) conductors, with sensor powered and output switching.
3. Record measurement.

**Pass Threshold:**
- Measured voltage ≥ 23.99 VDC AND ≤ 24.10 VDC

**Fail Threshold:**
- Measured voltage < 23.95 VDC (excessive drop, loose connection, or supply error) OR
- Measured voltage > 24.50 VDC (supply overvoltage or measurement error)

**Action on Fail:** If measured drop exceeds 0.01 VDC from source (greater than 2× calculated 0.00483 VDC), inspect and re-terminate all connections before proceeding.

### 3.3 Output Switching Check at Line Speed
**Procedure:**
1. Mount sensor head with registration mark in beam path at specified sensing distance per Keyence LV-N11N manual.
2. Adjust sensitivity and alignment per manufacturer instructions.
3. Run machine at normal operating line speed.
4. Place registration mark in sensor beam path; verify Black output sinks (logic low / ON) when mark is present.
5. Remove registration mark from beam path; verify Black output opens (high-impedance / OFF) when mark is absent.
6. Repeat for 100 consecutive mark detection cycles.

**Pass Threshold:**
- Stable toggling on every mark
- Response time ≤ 5 ms (within sensor specification)
- Zero missed marks over 100 cycles
- Zero false triggers over 100 cycles

**Fail Threshold:**
- Any missed detection
- Failure to sink (ON) or open (OFF)
- Output chatter or instability
- Response time > 5 ms

### 3.4 Documentation and Sign-Off
1. Record measured voltage at sensor head: _______ VDC
2. Record number of successful detection cycles: _______ / 100
3. Record any anomalies or deviations: _______
4. Technician signature and date: _______

---

## SECTION 4: CROSS-SECTION CONSISTENCY VERIFICATION

| Parameter          | Section 1 (Wiring) | Section 2 (Parts) | Section 3 (Commissioning) | Status |
|--------------------|---------------------|-------------------|---------------------------|--------|
| Supply voltage     | 24 VDC              | 24 VDC            | 24 VDC                    | ✓      |
| Voltage drop       | 0.00483 VDC         | —                 | 0.00483 VDC               | ✓      |
| Wire gauge         | 22 AWG              | 22 AWG            | —                         | ✓      |
| Part number        | LV-N11N             | LV-N11N           | LV-N11N                   | ✓      |
| Output type        | NPN open-collector  | NPN open-collector| NPN open-collector        | ✓      |
| Cable run          | 3 ft one-way        | 3 ft              | —                         | ✓      |

All parameters consistent across all sections.

---

## SECTION 5: ENGINEERING NOTES AND WARNINGS

### 5.1 Unverified Assumption (Critical)
The machine PCB input type (NPN-compatible/sourcing vs. PNP-compatible/sinking) is **NOT VERIFIED** from available documentation. This is the primary risk item. Do not energize the sensor output until the PCB input type is confirmed compatible with NPN open-collector (sinking) output.

### 5.2 EMC Considerations
- Route sensor cable minimum 2" from motor drives and VFD output cables
- Use shielded cable with drain wire; ground shield at PCB end only
- If EMI issues arise, consider adding a common-mode choke or ferrite core near the sensor end

### 5.3 Environmental Protection
- Paper dust accumulation on sensor lens will degrade performance; schedule periodic cleaning
- Ensure conduit fittings are sealed against dust ingress
- Verify ambient temperature at mounting location does not exceed sensor rating

### 5.4 Maintenance Access
- Mount sensor head with adjustable bracket for alignment
- Provide clearance for lens cleaning access
- Include test point or indicator LED for troubleshooting if available

### 5.5 Safety Classification
- This sensor is a process input, NOT a safety-rated device
- Do not use for e-stop, guard monitoring, or safety-critical functions
- For safety applications, use certified safety sensors with dual-channel architecture

---

END OF IMPLEMENTATION DOCUMENT

plan.plan:
=== IMPLEMENTATION PLAN: Keyence LV-N11N REGISTRATION-MARK SENSOR INTEGRATION ===

CONTEXT / UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTIONS (explicit, not asserted as fact):
- The machine PCB provides 24 VDC supply to the sensor; this is assumed because no authoritative machine schematic or I/O card datasheet was provided. Verify with the PCB drawing before energizing.
- The machine PCB digital input type (NPN vs PNP / sourcing vs sinking) is UNVERIFIED. The sensor specified is the LV-N11N, which is NPN open-collector. The wiring below assumes the PCB input accepts an NPN open-collector sinking output (sourcing input per IEC 61131-2 digital input practice). If the PCB actually requires a PNP/sourcing-output device, this pairing is incompatible and the sensor model must be changed to the PNP equivalent (e.g., LV-P11N or equivalent PNP variant) and the signal wiring revised accordingly. Do not finalize wiring until the PCB I/O datasheet confirms input category.

=== 1) WIRING SECTION ===
Supply voltage: 24 VDC (assumed from machine PCB; sensor rated 24 VDC).
Wire specification: 22 AWG stranded copper, 16.1 Ω per 1000 ft.
Cable run: 3 feet one-way (6 feet round-trip for voltage-drop arithmetic).
Voltage-drop arithmetic (shown exactly as requested):
  Drop = 2 × length × resistance × current
  Drop = 2 × 3 ft × (16.1 Ω / 1000 ft) × 0.050 A
  Drop = 2 × 3 × 0.0161 Ω/ft × 0.050 A
  Drop = 0.00483 VDC
Computed head voltage: 24.000 VDC − 0.00483 VDC = 23.995 VDC.
This drop (0.00483 VDC) is negligible relative to the 24 VDC supply; the sensor’s operating range accommodates it, but the value must be consistent everywhere.
Output type / matching: LV-N11N = NPN open-collector (verified from Keyence product/datasheet sources). The machine PCB input compatibility is the unverified item above. Wiring assignment (if NPN-compatible PCB input): Brown to +24 VDC (PCB supply), Blue to 0 V / common, Black to PCB digital input (sink). Shield/drain (if cable has shield) to PCB ground at the PCB end only; do not ground both ends.
Mechanical / protection: Route the 3-ft run inside 3/8" flexible conduit or equivalent; secure with clamps every 12 in; provide strain relief at both sensor head and PCB terminal block; keep wiring away from heat sources, moving parts, and paper dust/debris. Use ferrule terminals at the PCB terminal block.

=== 2) PARTS SECTION ===
Part number: Keyence LV-N11N (NPN open-collector, 24 VDC, laser registration-mark sensor).
Supply voltage: 24 VDC (matches assumed PCB supply and sensor specification; consistent with wiring section).
Output type: NPN open-collector (consistent with part number; unverified match to PCB input — see assumption).
Unit cost estimate: ~$400 USD for the LV-N11N sensor; ~$50 USD for 3 ft 22 AWG shielded cable, flex conduit, ferrules, strain relief, and mounting hardware; total estimated material cost ~$450 USD.
Accessories / verification: Keyence-compatible M8/M12 mounting bracket or MS-N11-style bracket (verify head interface); 3 ft 22 AWG stranded copper cable (if not using integral cable); terminal block; ferrule crimp terminals; multimeter for commissioning measurements.

=== 3) COMMISSIONING SECTION ===
Powered voltage check at the sensor head (measured at sensor connector, brown-to-blue, under load):
- Pass threshold: ≥ 23.99 VDC and ≤ 24.10 VDC (this incorporates the calculated 0.00483 V drop from the 24 VDC source, allowing minor connection tolerance).
- Fail threshold: < 23.95 VDC (indicating excessive drop, loose connection, or supply error) OR > 24.50 VDC (indicating supply overvoltage or measurement error).
Note: The 0.00483 V drop is documented; if measured drop exceeds ~0.01 VDC from source, inspect terminations.
Output switching check at line speed (machine at normal operating speed):
- Procedure: Place registration mark in beam path; verify Black output sinks (low / ON) with mark present and opens (high-impedance / OFF) with mark absent. Repeat for 100 consecutive cycles at normal line speed.
- Pass threshold: Stable toggling on every mark, response within sensor specification (< 1 ms typical, allow ≤ 5 ms for pass/fail), zero missed marks or false triggers over 100 cycles.
- Fail threshold: Any missed detection, failure to sink/open, chatter, or missed mark at line speed.
Consistency check across all sections: Supply = 24 VDC; Drop = 0.00483 VDC; Wire = 22 AWG; Part = LV-N11N; Output = NPN open-collector; Run length = 3 ft one-way.

=== ADDITIONAL ENGINEERING NOTES ===
- EMC: Keep sensor cable separated from motor drives and high-current lines; use shielded cable if available; ground shield at PCB end only.
- Maintenance / accessibility: Mount sensor head with adjustable bracket so the registration mark is within sensing distance; provide access for lens cleaning (paper dust can affect laser performance); include a manual test point or LED indicator if available.
- Safety / interlocks: The sensor signal should be treated as a process input, not a safety interlock, unless the machine’s risk assessment specifically requires it; if used for e-stop or guard monitoring, use a certified safety sensor and dual-channel architecture instead.
- Software / firmware: Confirm the machine control system interprets the NPN sinking signal correctly (likely a sourcing digital input expecting a low-level sink); if logic is inverted, adjust input logic or wiring—not the sensor.
- Calibration: After mechanical mounting, adjust distance/angle per Keyence LV-N11N manual; verify registration-mark size/contrast meets sensor spec; set sensitivity if adjustable; run the 100-cycle line-speed test to confirm.
success_criteria: The Keyence LV-N11N part number is installed with 24 VDC supply, 22 AWG stranded copper, and a 3-foot one-way cable run, and the voltage-drop calculation 2 × 3 ft × (16.1 Ω/1000 ft) × 0.050 A = 0.00483 VDC is documented and verified by measurement at commissioning.

The sensor head receives a measured voltage between 23.99 VDC and 24.10 VDC at the brown-to-blue connector under load, confirming the 0.00483 V drop is within tolerance and no excessive connection resistance exists.

The LV-N11N NPN open-collector output is wired to the machine PCB digital input only after the PCB input type is verified (unverified assumption noted); if the PCB requires PNP, the sensor is replaced with a PNP equivalent and wiring revised before final energization.
At normal line speed, the output switching check shows stable toggling with the registration mark over 100 consecutive cycles, with zero missed marks, zero false triggers, and response time ≤ 5 ms.

All wiring is routed in protected conduit with strain relief, secured every 12 in, shielded/drain terminated at the PCB end only, and protected from paper dust, heat, and mechanical stress per the installation plan.
Every figure repeated across sections agrees: supply = 24 VDC, drop = 0.00483 VDC, wire = 22 AWG, part = LV-N11N, output = NPN open-collector, and run length = 3 ft one-way.
